title: Claims Handler
description:
Job Title: Claims Handler

Location: Bristol (Hybrid - 3 days per week in the office)

Salary: Up to £35,000

Benefits: Hybrid working, professional qualification support (CII), long-term progression opportunities

About the Company:

This is an opportunity to join a well-established and growing specialist insurer with a strong reputation across financial lines, construction, accident & health, and affinity products. Backed by a major international parent group, the business combines the stability and support of a global insurer with the close-knit culture of a smaller regional team. With excellent staff retention and ambitious growth plans over the next few years, the business offers genuine long-term career development within a collaborative environment.

Role Summary:

This is an opportunity to join a busy claims function and manage insurance claims from first notification through to settlement or resolution.

You'll take ownership of claim outcomes, work closely with customers, brokers, adjusters and suppliers, and build broader technical exposure across coverage, liability, reserving and claims decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:
- Manage claims from FNOL through to resolution: Build end-to-end claims experience while taking ownership of outcomes
- Review policy terms, coverage and claim documentation: Develop stronger technical judgement around coverage and liability decisions
- Communicate with customers and brokers: Build trusted relationships while providing clear and professional claims updates
- Liaise with TPAs, adjusters and suppliers: Gain exposure to the wider claims process and external stakeholders
- Maintain accurate, audit-ready claim files: Strengthen your understanding of regulatory, data and compliance requirements
- Monitor reserves, indemnity spend and settlement strategy: Develop commercial awareness and intelligent claims decision-making

Requirements:
- Experience or technical knowledge of insurance claims, including the claims lifecycle from FNOL through to settlement
- Understanding of policy wordings, coverage principles and liability assessment, with familiarity with Civil Procedure Rules and the litigation process
- Awareness of FCA requirements, Consumer Duty, data protection and fair customer outcomes
- Confident communication, organisation and claims-system skills, with the ability to manage workloads and escalate complex matters appropriately

If this role isn't quite right, it's still worth speaking to one of our specialist team - we may be working on something that hasn't hit the market yet.

Related Job Titles: Claims Advisor, Claims Technician, Claims Adjuster, Claims Specialist, Insurance Claims Handler

title: Personal Injury Paralegal
description:
Personal Injury Paralegal

Bristol

Salary up to £30,000 DOE

Yolk Recruitment is supporting a highly regarded national law firm with the recruitment of an experienced Personal Injury Paralegal to join its established claimant injury team in Bristol. This is an excellent opportunity for a Personal Injury Paralegal or experienced PI Case Handler who is confident managing their own caseload and wants to develop their career within a supportive and well-established legal environment.

The successful Personal Injury Paralegal will manage a varied caseload of injury claims, including matters involving vulnerable road users such as cyclists, pedestrians and motorcyclists, alongside minor to moderate head injury claims. You will handle claims through both the MOJ Portal and litigation process, with responsibility for progressing matters from initial instruction through to conclusion.

The role offers hybrid working, with two days per week based in the Bristol office and the remaining days working from home.

This is what you will be doing

As a Personal Injury Paralegal, your duties and responsibilities will include:-
- Managing your own caseload of claimant personal injury matters, including claims valued up to £25,000.
- Progressing claims both within and outside the MOJ Portal, including pre-litigation and litigated matters.
- Handling Fast Track claims through the litigation process, including issuing proceedings, complying with Court Directions and progressing matters towards Trial.
- Liaising regularly with clients, insurers, expert witnesses, solicitors and other third parties while managing client expectations.
- Maintaining accurate case records, meeting service standards and participating in regular case and risk assessment meetings.

The experience you will bring to the team

You will bring the following experience to the Personal Injury team:-
- Previous experience managing your own claimant personal injury caseload.
- A strong working knowledge of the MOJ Portal and Fast Track personal injury claims.
- Experience of litigation, including issuing proceedings, complying with Court Directions and progressing cases towards Trial.
- Strong communication, organisation and client-management skills, with the ability to prioritise a busy caseload effectively.
- A law degree, CILEx qualification or equivalent would be advantageous but is not essential where you can demonstrate relevant practical experience.

This is what you will get in return

You will receive a competitive salary up to £30,000 depending on experience, alongside a comprehensive benefits package including:
- Hybrid working, with only two days per week required in the Bristol office.
- Generous annual leave and employee welfare benefits.
- Health cash plan and gym/lifestyle benefits.
- Work-life balance initiatives and a flexible approach to workplace dress.
- Employee recognition and referral schemes.
- Training, development and routes towards further legal qualification.
- The opportunity to develop your career within an established national law firm and experienced claimant personal injury team.

Are you up to the challenge?

If you're a Personal Injury Paralegal ready to take the next step in your career, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today or get in touch to find out more. All enquiries will be handled in the strictest confidence by Yolk Recruitment. If you are looking to pursue the next step in your career with a highly regarded law firm, we encourage you to apply by contacting Oliver Coodye on or alternatively send your CV Yolk Recruitment is an equal opportunities employer and embraces diversity in our workforce. We employ the best people for the job at hand and actively encourage applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, age, race, religion, sexual orientation, disability, educational background, parental status, gender identity or any other protected characteristic. We champion and celebrate diversity at Yolk allowing our team to bring their whole selves to work. Please note, whilst we do our best to contact all candidates, due to the high number of applications we receive we cannot guarantee this for every role. If you have not heard anything from us within 7 days of applying - then unfortunately you have been unsuccessful. Please keep an eye on our website for more opportunities.

title: Peripatetic Service Coordinator - Mental Health
description:
Please note that the closing date for this post has been extended to 14th October to allow more time for applications.

We are looking for an experienced and compassionate leader to join our Mental Health Services as a Peripatetic Service Coordinator, supporting teams across Bristol and South Gloucestershire. This is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference to the lives of people with complex mental health needs while supporting and developing high-performing teams.

As a Service Coordinator, you will lead teams to support people with complex mental health needs to achieve their goals, build independence, and develop the skills and confidence needed to live fulfilling lives within their communities. You will help people build resilience, develop practical life skills, strengthen community connections, and take greater control of their future through person-centred support.

You will be an inspirational and supportive leader with excellent communication and listening skills, able to motivate, develop and empower colleagues to deliver outstanding support. You will have a strong understanding of person-centred practice and a commitment to promoting positive mental health, wellbeing and recovery-focused support.

You will ensure services operate safely, effectively and in line with relevant legislation, regulations and organisational standards, while evidencing positive outcomes for the people we support.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing the day-to-day operation of services, including rota planning and resource allocation, to ensure people receive the right support at the right time.
- Supporting teams to co-produce and regularly review support plans, risk assessments and positive risk management strategies.
- Providing regular supervision, coaching and performance support to team members, while ensuring training and development needs are met.
- Contributing to referrals, assessments and service transition planning.
- Monitoring service budgets and expenditure in line with organisational expectations.
- Providing direct, hands-on support when required and leading by example in delivering high-quality care and support.

The successful candidate will:
- Demonstrate strong leadership skills, with experience of supervising, leading or coordinating a team.
- Be highly organised and able to prioritise competing demands in a fast-paced environment.
- Have experience supporting people with complex mental health needs and a sound understanding of recovery-focused practice.
- Be confident in responding to people who are experiencing acute mental illness, in dynamic risk management and developing escalation plans to ensure that people receive the support that they need.
- Have knowledge of mental health services, legislation and best practice, including experience of trauma-informed approaches.
- Be flexible to work across a seven-day service, including a variety of shift patterns as required.

In return, you will have the opportunity to lead dedicated teams, shape service delivery, and support people on their recovery journey within a values-driven organisation committed to learning, inclusion and continuous improvement.

At Milestones Trust we recognise that without the hard work, commitment and passion of our staff, we wouldn't be the charity that we are today. In return, we are committed to rewarding you with a competitive pay and benefits package including:
- 34 days' annual leave, including recognised public holidays
- Learning and development to support your career growth
- Nationally recognised qualifications, from entry level care to management
- Flexible working, with rotas provided in advance
- Occupational Sick Pay after two years, increasing with service
- Health Cash Plan after probation, offering at least £695 cashback for health treatments (dental, optical, therapies, maternity/paternity, prescriptions)
- Enhanced maternity and paternity pay
- Free enhanced DBS check
- Dayforce Wallet, giving you access to your earnings before payday
- Employee referral scheme with financial rewards
- Employee Assistance Programme from day one, offering confidential 24/7 support
- Company pension scheme to help grow your retirement savings

We pride ourselves with being able to offer staff opportunities to develop and progress their careers within the Trust.

- General Office Tasks: Assist with general office administration including managing staff refreshments, handling post, and answering calls.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Experience in an Accounts Assistant or Finance Assistant role.
- Strong understanding of Accounts Payable and/or Accounts Receivable processes.
- Excellent numerical accuracy and attention to detail.
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel.
- Ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks.
- Excellent communication skills.

Desirable:
- Experience in property management or real estate finance.
- Knowledge of service charge accounting.
- Familiarity with property management or accounting software (e.g., Xero, ApprovalMax, Re-Leased).

Personal Attributes:
- Proactive and organised, comfortable with varied tasks.
- Reliable and trustworthy with strong ownership of duties.

- Collaborative with a "can-do" attitude.

description: Please note, we cannot offer a Certificate of Sponsorship for this role. If you currently require a visa to work in the UK, there must be a minimum of 14 months remaining until the expiry date. If you do not disclose your expiry date within your application, it may not be considered. Please only provide the expiry date and not your share code within your application. We are seeking an experienced Senior Administrator to join our Administrative team. You will support the Community Integrated Neighbourhood Team for North & West Bristol. You will work as part of a team within our locality coordination office, be supportive to the Locality Managers, the wider clinical teams, the admin team and be familiar with patient data base systems. The successful candidate will hold qualifications in Numeracy and Literacy level 2 qualification or equivalent, have a high level of IT Literacy and preferably hold an NVQ level 3 in Business Administration. Previous experience within a healthcare setting is desirable, but not essential. Hours are between 8am and 8pm, 7 days per week, on a rota basis. This role is in person, based predominantly in NBICC, but will be required to visit our other bases in Horfield and Shirehampton. If you are a team player with excellent admin skills and enjoy a challenge, we look forward to hearing from you. Previous applicants need not apply. Lead and manage the review, coordination and allocation of referrals within the locality working closely with other servcies to achieve timely patient hospital discharges and efficent care allocation. Support to Managers including proactively arranging meetings, booking appointments, minute taking at meetings, new initiatives, projects, audits, staffing trackers (recruitment, terminations, SRP's, Bank etc) and budgets. Coordination of team capacity and staffing rotas. Lead and manage community team administrators. To work collaboratively with the other locality administrators to imbed consistent and high quality support and systems across the service. Responsible for training and development of Band 3 administration staff within the team and to provide ad hoc training and support across the whole team when new initiatives are implemented. Plan and organise a broad range of complex activities, reprioritising own workload at very short notice as urgent issues or new tasks arise. To provide short term support and coordinate cover within the team in the absence of Band 3 administration staff e.g. sickness cover. To establish good communication systems within the locality, ensuring a culture of openness and efficiency. Provision of support and escalation of issues that arise within the teams regarding referrers, patients and relatives and managing or escalating appropriately as the situation demands. Please read the attached Job Description and Person Specification for full details of the role before applying. If you refer to qualifications or employment within your supporting statement, that has not been included in your Qualifications, Training or Employment History, this information may be discounted.
